attributes.title: TICKET-002: Enforce confirmation-proof lifecycle
attributes.body:
# TICKET-002: Enforce confirmation-proof lifecycle

## Observable goal

Learners can confirm email ownership only with the current valid proof, while failed proof attempts leave account state private and unchanged. A valid proof confirms a blocked learner without restoring ordinary sign-in eligibility.

## Source IDEA, EPIC, version, and scenario IDs

IDEA-009/v003; EPIC-001/v002; SCENARIO-004, SCENARIO-005, SCENARIO-006, SCENARIO-007, SCENARIO-008, SCENARIO-012.

## Acceptance evidence

`spec/requests/confirmations_spec.rb` proves valid-current confirmation (SCENARIO-004); invalid, expired, used, and superseded proofs leave account state unchanged (SCENARIO-005 through SCENARIO-008); and a blocked learner is confirmed without mutation of the blocked state (SCENARIO-012). TICKET-011 supplies the persisted block state and the request proof that correct blocked credentials cannot start a session.

## Dependencies

TICKET-011

## Difficulty (1-5)

3

## Estimate (ideal days, at most 2)

1.5

## Risks

Token handling can disclose private account state or accept an old, expired, or used proof. Confirmation must not clear or otherwise alter the blocked state supplied by TICKET-011.

## External actions

Configure the production confirmation URL host and email delivery.

## Allowed scope

Devise Confirmable token lifecycle, confirmation-controller outcome, confirmation result copy, mailer URL configuration, and focused confirmation specs. No blocked-state persistence or authentication-policy implementation, resend form, registration flow, block/unblock administration, recovery proof lifecycle, or production mail-provider setup.

<!-- product-factory-ticket-id: TICKET-002 -->

attributes.title: TICKET-011: Establish blocked-account sign-in eligibility
attributes.body:
# TICKET-011: Establish blocked-account sign-in eligibility

## Observable goal

A persisted blocked account can confirm email ownership without becoming eligible for ordinary sign-in; blocked credentials receive the existing generic sign-in rejection and create no session.

## Source IDEA, EPIC, version, and scenario IDs

IDEA-009/v003; EPIC-001/v002; SCENARIO-012.

## Acceptance evidence

Focused model and request specs prove that a blocked, unconfirmed learner can be confirmed without clearing the blocked state, then cannot sign in with correct credentials and receives no authenticated session. The rejected response matches the generic invalid-credentials outcome.

## Dependencies

none

## Difficulty (1-5)

3

## Estimate (ideal days, at most 2)

1

## Risks

An authentication override could accidentally bypass Devise Confirmable or expose a blocked state through a distinct failure message. Existing-session invalidation is intentionally outside this ticket and remains TICKET-004's responsibility.

## External actions

The administrator-owned blocking system must use the agreed persisted block/unblock transition; no administration interface is included here.

## Allowed scope

The `users` blocked-state migration, `User` block predicate and Devise sign-in eligibility hook, generic failure mapping, and focused model/request specs. No confirmation-proof lifecycle changes, block/unblock UI, existing-session invalidation, or recovery behavior.

<!-- product-factory-ticket-id: TICKET-011 -->
